doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Straw hats, uniforms and the band's volunteer spirit
summary: Tuba and trombone slide hit the hats, so hats are worn only for photographs; he stresses the band plays free and wants it easy for them.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I’ve always insisted that the straw hats be worn. And it’s been, I think a boon to us because our publicity is very good. The pictures of us in the Alumni Review for example with the hats on are terrific, it’s a uniform thing. But lately I’m getting a lot of resistance to wearing the hats. And two sources. Gordy Bourns says, “When I wear the hat I can’t play the tuba, the tuba hits it.” And Phil Mead, his trombone slide hits the hat. And that is absolutely right, those are justifiable complaints. So what we’ll do, I’ve told them that you don’t have to wear the hats except when we’re being photographed. That’s the impression that I want to convey to readers of the Alumni Review, that we’re a uniformed band and all. So I’m going to talk about it tonight with them at our little dinner. But I have this — the people who come to hear us at Hamilton, be it the reunion class that we’re playing for at the banquet or people at the cookout or anyplace, I think they are not that impressed by the fine degree of improvement in our music over last year, but they are impressed by the uniformed appearance with the straw hats. And we may think we can play better, and something we do, but I don’t think the audience hears much of that really, to tell you the truth. I think we’re playing as well as we’re ever going to play. So I say, “Please put the hats on when the photographer is out there clicking.

But for the guys that have this physical disability, they can’t play their horn, you’ve got to be — they’re not getting paid, they come up here and they do this for nothing every year, and I want to make it as easy for them.
Yeah. It doesn’t want to become annoying. All right. Well say hi to the rest of the fellas for me.
I’m going to tell them it was not bad.
I’ll scare Donny Andre and I’ll say, “Wait until you get your chance to do this.” That was very nice, Monk, thanks for asking me.
